editions.text: Yesterday marked the busiest day in the past week, with 268 feeder visits and 21 species recorded, well above the seven-day average of 97 visits and 12 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees were the dominant visual presences, maintaining their status as regulars present every day this week. The station’s new seed feeder and treat bowl, installed over the past week, coincided with a significant increase in visitor diversity and frequency. A Black-capped Chickadee provided the station’s first confident visual record, joining a list that included a Common Gallinule, also a first visual for this location. The day closed with a final auditory detection of a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at 20:30. The high volume of detections, particularly from Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals, reflects the continued presence of the new microphone installed on September 13.

The Tufted Titmouse arrived six minutes before sunrise, opening the feeder before the light fully took hold. By the time the Carolina Wren began its loud calling in the early hour, the Titmouse had already logged a dozen visits. Tufted Titmice accounted for sixty-one of the day’s two hundred and ten visual records, alongside Carolina Chickadees and a small contingent of Mourning Doves. A single Northern Cardinal appeared at 07:54.
